prompt.context: Our client is Lactose King, a premium ice cream restaurant chain with approximately 3,000 locations throughout the United States. While they've enjoyed consistent profitability and are an industry leader in direct-to-consumer ice cream sales, their revenue has been stagnant over the past few years. Lactose King operates under a simple business model of owning and operating all of their own stores, procuring ingredients from various suppliers throughout the country, and processing/serving the ice cream at individual locations. They serve only soft-serve ice cream and related products (milkshakes, ice cream sandwiches, etc.). Revenue last year was $250K per store, totaling $750M across 3,000 stores.
prompt.question: What can Lactose King do to improve their gross revenue? Specifically, they would like to improve gross revenue by 33% within 1 year, targeting $1B total revenue.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any anticipated market growth in the ice cream industry next year?
clarifying_info.a: No anticipated market growth in any demographic next year.

clarifying_info.q: If Lactose King introduces a new product, will it cannibalize existing sales?
clarifying_info.a: 1/3 of existing sales are likely to be cannibalized through the introduction of the new sugar-free ice cream.

exhibits.title: Customer Breakdown
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing 2016 US Direct-to-Consumer Ice Cream Buyers by Age, broken down by company (Lactose King, Sugar Shack, Heavenly Ice Cream, Delly's Dairy, Other) across five age demographics (<18, 18-32, 33-45, 46-60, >60). Each age group bar shows percentage share held by each company. Market size figures are shown for each age group.

exhibits.title: Ice Cream Store Criteria
exhibits.shows: A chart listing six criteria (Price, Low Calorie, Store Appearance, Taste, Customer Service, Product Variety) with two dimensions for each: Importance for 18-32 Ice Cream Buyers and Lactose King's Performance Compared to Competition (ranked worst to best).

exhibits.title: Anticipated Market Share for Sugar-Free Ice Cream
exhibits.shows: A table showing the anticipated US market share Lactose King would capture for a new sugar-free ice cream product, broken down by age demographic.

framework: Improve existing ice cream sales: marketing campaigns, loyalty programs, pricing strategy
Expand geographically: open new US locations or expand outside the United States
Offer a new product: add a dessert or non-dessert item to the menu
Utilize a new sales channel: sell through grocery stores or other retail channels
Target a new customer demographic: identify underserved age groups with high potential
Assess consumer preferences: understand what drives purchase decisions in target segments

questions.prompt: Which age demographic should Lactose King target to improve revenue? Use Exhibit 1.
questions.guidance: A strong candidate evaluates three factors for each age group: (1) total market size, (2) percentage NOT already held by LK (room for growth), and (3) percentage held by 'Other' (market fragmentation/ease of capture). The 18-32 segment wins on all three: largest market at $1.2B, LK holds only 10% (90% upside), and 25% is fragmented among 'Other'. Note the market size numbers use different units ($10M vs $1.2B etc.) — candidates must catch this. After identifying 18-32, candidate should brainstorm what matters to that demographic before moving to Exhibit 2.

questions.prompt: Given Exhibit 2, what is the most important area for Lactose King to improve to win the 18-32 demographic?
questions.guidance: The candidate should identify criteria where importance is high AND LK performance is low — the gap represents addressable opportunity. 'Low Calorie' is the clear answer: it is rated 'Very' important by 18-32 buyers, and LK performs 'Low' compared to competition. Price is also Low performance, but only 'Somewhat' important to this group. Taste is Very important but LK already performs well there. Candidate should recommend addressing the low-calorie gap, e.g., by introducing sugar-free or reduced-calorie options.

questions.prompt: A small company going out of business will license Lactose King the right to make and sell sugar-free ice cream for next to nothing. Using Exhibit 3, estimate how much additional net revenue this would generate for Lactose King next year. (Clarifying info available: no market growth; 1/3 of existing sales will be cannibalized.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply each age group's total market size by LK's anticipated sugar-free share, then sum. Then subtract cannibalization of existing LK revenue. Final net revenue from sugar-free should be approximately $400K above the current $750M baseline, reaching ~$1.15B and satisfying the 33% growth target.

math.setup: For each age group: (market size) × (LK anticipated sugar-free share). Sum all age groups to get gross new revenue from sugar-free. Then subtract cannibalization: 1/3 × (LK's current revenue of $750M). Net new revenue = gross sugar-free revenue - cannibalized revenue.
math.answer: Net additional revenue of $400M, bringing total to $1.15B (53% growth, surpassing the $1B / 33% target).

brainstorming.prompt: Now that we've identified the 18-32 year old market and the low-calorie gap, what might be important to consider when targeting this new demographic with a sugar-free/low-calorie product?

categories.name: Product development
ideas: Formulate a sugar-free soft-serve recipe that maintains premium taste
Ensure texture and quality match or exceed the original product
License or develop proprietary low-calorie ingredients
Consider reduced-fat or dairy-free variants to broaden appeal

categories.name: Marketing and branding
ideas: Digital and social media campaigns targeting 18-32 cohort
Influencer partnerships with health and fitness personalities
Transparent calorie/nutrition labeling in-store and online

categories.name: Operations
ideas: Train staff on new product preparation and quality standards
Manage dual recipe inventory (original + sugar-free) without cross-contamination
Assess capacity of existing equipment or need for new machines
Prevent cannibalizing premium brand perception by maintaining quality standards

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Determine whether sugar-free commands a premium or discount vs. original
Evaluate price sensitivity of 18-32 buyers (only 'somewhat' important per Exhibit 2)
Consider introductory pricing to drive trial

categories.name: Channel and distribution
ideas: Promote in-store point-of-sale materials at all 3,000 locations
Leverage mobile app or loyalty program for targeted promotions
Explore whether sugar-free variant could accelerate grocery channel entry

recommendation: Introduce a sugar-free ice cream product by licensing the recipe from the small company going out of business, at minimal upfront cost
Target the 18-32 age demographic, where LK currently holds only 10% of a $1.2B market, by addressing their top unmet need: low-calorie options

This initiative is projected to generate $650M in gross new revenue; after accounting for 1/3 cannibalization of existing sales ($250M), net new revenue is ~$400M, bringing total revenue to $1.15B — a 53% increase that exceeds the 33% / $1B target
risks: Cannibalization risk: 1/3 of existing customers may switch to the sugar-free product, reducing margin if sugar-free costs more to produce
Brand dilution: introducing a 'diet' product could undermine the premium positioning of the original recipe
Operational complexity: running dual product lines may strain kitchen capacity, staff training, and ingredient logistics
Taste/quality risk: if the licensed recipe does not meet LK's premium standard, it could damage the brand
next_steps: Conduct taste tests and quality validation of the licensed sugar-free recipe before full rollout
Develop a targeted marketing plan for the 18-32 segment, emphasizing digital and social channels
Design a phased launch (pilot in select markets, then national rollout) to manage operational risk
Track cannibalization rate closely post-launch and adjust pricing or marketing if it exceeds the 1/3 assumption
